full_judgment:
2. Short facts for disposal of the Rule are, that the opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 as plaintiffs instituted title suit No. 182 of 1997 for declaration of title and recovery of possession. Trial Court dismissed the suit but on appeal there from the appellate Court decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 27-6-2000. Then, a civil revision presented against the judgment and decree by the judgment debtor was discharged. Civil petition for leave to appeal there from was also dismissed by the Appellate Division on 16-7-2003. 

 3. Decree holder then put the decree in execution in title execution No. 7 of 2003 for possession. Petitioner then unsuccessfully tried to get the execution proceeding struck off. A revision presented against the order of the trial Court refusing to strike out the execution was also discharged on hearing on 20-4-2005. 

 4. Meanwhile, the judgment debtor instituted title suit No. 14 of 2004 against the decree holder for perpetual injunction for restraining him from taking possession of the suit land. In the execution proceeding, he made an application under Order XXI, rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for stay of further proceedings of the execution case. The executing Court however, allowed the application and granted stay execution of further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of title suit No. 14 of 2004. 

 5. Against the order of stay, the decree holder made a revision application before the district Judge at Brahmanbaria. Additional District Judge, Second Court hearing the revision was pleased to allow the revision and set aside the order dated 4-7-2005 and directed executing Court to proceed with the execution expeditiously. 

 7. In the aforesaid circumstances, the application made under rule XXI of order 29 must be need to be misconceived and tortuous on the part of the judgment debtor to stall the execution proceeding. How the executing Court failed not to take notice of every attempt of the judgment debtor failed up to this Court to deprive the decree holder of the fruits of the decree by stalling execution of the decree. In the facts and circumstances, order of stay granted by the executing Court was not legal and proper and the revision Court having set aside such illegal order committed no error of law occasioning failure of justice calling for interference by this Division.
